The first workflow execution claim precedes acquisition of its environment lease. That claim has a live `workflow:<operationId>` execution holder and consumed proposal approvals, but NULL `lease_scope` and `fence_token`. The existing source-retention guard requires a recorded live environment fence, while the later plan-publication binder cannot run until after source capture and retention. This packet binds the first real worker lease before source capture.

`LeasesPort.acquire` accepts optional internal worker metadata containing the operation id and the stored proposal digest. The real acquisition activity supplies this metadata only after loading an actual operation and checking the exact environment scope. Reconcile passes supply no operation metadata. This is worker context, not a public approval input or identity proof. No Temporal command or historical workflow ordering changes.

The native adapter acquires or renews the actual lease and calls the native binder in one database transaction. It locks the environment lease before the operation. Binding requires an exact tenant and environment, unchanged proposal digest, a running unexpired operation, a live execution claim held by `workflow:<id>`, and a live unreleased environment lease with the exact non-NULL workspace, worker holder and fence token. Worker holders retain the existing `worker:<validatedWorkerId>:<operationId>` shape. The final conditional write executes after the operation lock, so cancellation or execution expiry committed during a lock wait is visible. It accepts only a fully NULL recorded pair or the exact already recorded pair; partial pairs and mismatched fences refuse. A refusal rolls back newly acquired leases or attempted lease extension.

A repeated native acquisition for the same exact operation and live worker holder renews and reuses the existing fence. This handles a lost activity acknowledgement without making the operation's recorded fence stale. Plain and reconcile acquisitions keep the repository's existing fence-increment semantics. Released, expired or taken-over recorded fences cannot be replaced by the binder. The existing human review flow releases the environment lease, suspends execution, opens a new approval round and clears the claim; a separate approved claim resets the recorded pair before a new fence can be bound. The binder neither claims execution, changes status, issues grants nor approves/reapproves/consumes human decisions.

Definitive binding refusals become the existing non-retryable `StepFailedError` in the native execution adapter. A stale live-fence assertion retains the existing `LeaseLostError` mapping. Unclassified database failures remain retryable. Source, artifact, resource, grant and approval guards are unchanged. The later plan-publication binder remains as its existing custody check; this packet does not expand it or add an alternative source authority.

The new suite `first source worker lease binding [postgres]` contains 24 named expanded cases. `ZENITH_TEST_FIRST_SOURCE_LEASE_REQUIRED=1` requires `PG_URL` and canonical registered schema 13 before hooks or pool creation. The primary success case starts with an actual native human-approval row and a real claim without any environment lease, invokes the real worker acquisition body with native store ports, then uses the default owning source runtime to capture and retain the canonical source and read it through an independent native pool. No prebinding or fake SQL/source store is used. Inaccessible unused non-store ports prove that lease acquisition does not invoke product or credential IO.

GitHub HTTP and archive replies, the discarded acknowledgement and the human role supplied to the native approval fixture are modeled. The review-cycle plan is a validated source-bound normalized fixture; it is not raw OpenTofu engine provenance. The tests do not prove live browser approval, Temporal delivery/identity, cloud provider mutation or Docker/package behavior. Refusal fixtures alter only their random scoped native operation or lease state, retain consumed approval rows unchanged, and prove rollback and non-retry classification. Two tests observe the exact operation-lock waiter and blocker from a third PostgreSQL backend before committing cancellation or execution expiry.

The six owned paths are four production files (`controlplane/db/repos/operations.ts`, `execution/platform.ts`, `execution/ports.ts`, `execution/steps.ts`), the new native regression file and this handoff. Existing model and native platform/step tests were inspected and left unchanged. Root owns mandatory gate registration for every literal identity and the required flag, canonical native PostgreSQL execution with zero required-case skips, compiler checks and actual Temporal workflow replay/delivery verification. No absence-of-PostgreSQL result can satisfy this suite. Outside-owned followups include that gate registration and root runtime verification; packaged, plan-artifact dispatch and prior R1/R2 fixture packets remain separate and frozen.
